html:
SMTO-UI-0038 — Hidden dots can't be saved as a password or key

GUID: 6fe04eb0-3f18-4478-b7f6-873aa2d34fd8
Slug: ui-parameter-mask-rejected
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • The value you're saving contains dots (••••) that SMTO uses to hide secrets on screen. Saving them would replace your real password or key with dots, so SMTO stopped. Your saved value hasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Value tab, find the dots (••••) and type or paste the real password, key or other value in their place, then select Save. The dots only stand in for a hidden value on screen, so the real text has to be there to save it.
  2. If you didn't mean to change a value you revealed, select Hide, then Discard value changes, and save your other edits. Hiding the value leaves the saved one exactly as it is, while your other changes are kept.
  3. If you copied the value from another screen, copy it again from where the real value is kept, not from a screen that shows dots. Copying from a hidden display copies the dots, not the secret.

What success looks like

  • The parameter shows "Saved" and the value box no longer reports the dots.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Never send the real password or key itself.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Parameter Store save rejected value_json because it contains the display mask "••••", which would overwrite the stored secret with its redacted preview.

What this means

  • The proposed raw parameter value contains a recognized redaction mask. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • The proposed raw parameter value contains a recognized redaction mask.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect whether the edit reused a display projection or explicitly revealed value.

How to fix it

  • parameter_editor.js collectParameterPayload() throws ui_parameter_mask_rejected when a new or revealed value_json contains "••••" in any key or string. Replace masked text with the real secret, or use Hide ("Discard value changes") to omit value_json and keep the stored value.
  • Reveal and enter the actual intended value, or hide it to keep the saved value unchanged.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The save contains the intended real value, or hidden saved fields remain unchanged.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
